provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-07-24T09 UTC: the Sun's centre is 2.24 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.56 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 96%, Earth in view 96%, both 91% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 276 Wh).
Longest darkness 15 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 424 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Darkest spell from 2029-08-05T03 UTC (15 h): terrain 8.8 km away blocks it (bearing 25 deg: skyline 1.47 deg, centre of the body at 1.20 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2029-08-06T19 UTC (14 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 146 deg, horizon -1.40 deg).
